findings.rule: Tokens: one typeface (Inter, owner decision 2026-09-22) — the one `field` token
findings.problem: `field` spreads only size/weight from sys.type.body and has no fontFamily. Inter is applied only inside `T` (withInter); no TextInput goes through T and there is no global default font, so every text field in scope (Poruke composer AgreementChat.tsx:300, AI composer AiConversationShell.tsx:287, support fields/pill SupportPresentation.tsx:256/294, Dogovor problem form, name, worker profile, search MarketplacePresentation.tsx:178, calendar CalendarControls.tsx:32, safety) draws typed text and placeholders in Roboto/SF next to Inter labels. It also passes fontWeight, which interFont.ts says must be removed once the face is chosen.
findings.fix: In tokens.ts `import { withInter } from '../interFont'` and define `export const field = { ...fieldBox, ...withInter(sys.type.body), color: sys.color.ink }` (Inter-Regular, no fontWeight). Apply withInter(...) to the input styles that build their own text: AgreementChat.tsx:300, AiConversationShell.tsx:287, SupportPresentation.tsx:294, MarketplacePresentation.tsx:178, CalendarControls.tsx:32.

verdict.evidence:
Confirmed. At ecb0f13, src/ui/system/tokens.ts:197 builds `field` as `{ ...fieldBox, ...sys.type.body, color }`. `sys.type.body` is `{ fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24, fontWeight: '400' }` (src/theme/tokens.ts:122) and has no fontFamily. Inter is only applied by `T` (src/ui/Text.tsx:53, via withInter in src/ui/interFont.ts:41-46). There is no defaultProps or global font anywhere in src, app.json or app.config.js; the expo-font plugin only bundles the files. So every in-scope TextInput draws its typed text and placeholder in Roboto/SF. The auth screens are not affected: they use their own AuthField.

The proposed token change is correct. In an isolated extract of ecb0f13, `field` flattens to fontFamily 'Inter-Regular' with no fontWeight. There is no import cycle, because interFont only imports react-native. No test mocks StyleSheet or reads fonts. 25 affected suites / 785 tests pass before and after, and tsc shows no errors in the patched files.

The fix list is incomplete, though. It leaves out the safety input it names itself (SafetyScreen.tsx:145) and several other inputs that build their own text. Also, WorkerProfilePresentation.tsx:334 `count` puts fontWeight '700' on top of `field`. After the token change, Android would draw that as a synthetic bold of Inter-Regular unless `count` is wrapped too.
verdict.fix:
1. tokens.ts: `import { withInter } from '../interFont';` and `export const field = { ...fieldBox, ...withInter(sys.type.body), color: sys.color.ink } satisfies TextStyle;`. This gives Inter-Regular with no fontWeight, and it covers the Dogovor problem form, name, group, worker profile/AI, the offer notes, FactValueEditors, AgreementActions and the Support fields.

2. Wrap each input style that builds its own text in `withInter({...})`, keeping its own sizes:
   - AgreementChat.tsx:300 `input`
   - AiConversationShell.tsx:287 `input`
   - SupportPresentation.tsx:294 `pillInput`
   - MarketplacePresentation.tsx:178 `input`

   Also these, which the report missed:
   - SafetyScreen.tsx:145 `const input`
   - TaskQaScreen.tsx:230 `const input`
   - DiscoveryPresentation.tsx:281 `input`
   - src/app/(app)/pregled-zadatka.tsx:449 `input`
   - ApplicationSelectionPresentation.tsx:529 `amountInput` (sys.type.price becomes Inter-Bold, tabular-nums kept)

3. CalendarControls.tsx:32 and LocationControls.tsx:19 are exactly `{...fieldBox, ...sys.type.body, color}`. Either use `field` there or wrap them in withInter.

4. WorkerProfilePresentation.tsx:334: `count: withInter({ width: 88, textAlign: 'center', fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 26, fontWeight: '700', fontVariant: ['tabular-nums'] })`. It overrides field's face with Inter-Bold. Without this, the capacity number becomes synthetic-bold Inter-Regular.

5. Do not touch src/ui/auth/AuthControls.tsx (locked).

This is style only: no guard, call or test intent changes, and no new dependency. Take an emulator screenshot of the pill composers (AgreementChat, AI, Support) to confirm the Inter metrics fit the 48px pills.

findings.rule: Layout: no raw layout values; one vertical scroll container per screen
findings.problem: The availability panel wraps AvailabilityForm (which owns a vertical ScrollView and a pinned save footer) in `<View style={{minHeight:650}}>` inside WorkerProfileFrame's own ScrollView. The form root (`flex: 1`) resolves to exactly 650 px, so its inner ScrollView gets 650 minus the footer while its content (Mogu odmah, 7 day rows ≥56, Posebni datumi, Dodaj izuzetak ≈830 px) is taller; a vertical ScrollView nested in a scrollable vertical ScrollView without nestedScrollEnabled takes no drags on Android, so Posebni datumi/Dodaj izuzetak cannot be scrolled to on typical phones. The save footer ('Primeni na pregled profila') sits mid-page at y≈650 instead of the screen foot, and insets double (frame padding 20 + form paddingHorizontal 20 → 240 px of content at 320 dp).
findings.fix: Host the panel as profil/dostupnost.tsx:58 does: a non-scrolling frame (CalendarScreen with title/back and scroll={false}, or a WorkerProfileFrame option that renders children without its ScrollView) with <AvailabilityForm … candidateMode /> as the direct flex child; delete the minHeight:650 View; put the error line and 'Proveri stanje razgovora' in that frame's footer.

verdict.evidence: The defect is real and in scope, but the report overstates it: razgovor.tsx:187 does put AvailabilityForm inside a raw `<View style={{minHeight:650}}>` inside WorkerProfileFrame's ScrollView (WorkerProfilePresentation.tsx:47-48, padding 20 at :305), and the form has its own vertical ScrollView (AvailabilityForm.tsx:442-443, paddingHorizontal sys.space.lg=20 at :559). That makes two vertical scroll containers, a 240-px text column at 320 dp (280 on /profil/dostupnost), and a save footer (AvailabilityForm.tsx:538) that scrolls inline under "Dodaj izuzetak" instead of staying at the screen foot. However, minHeight is only a floor: I laid out this exact tree with the Yoga that RN 0.86.3 ships, configured as Fabric does (YGErrataAll, ScrollView baseVertical style). The wrapper, the form root, the inner viewport and the inner content all come out equal (805.8 px, inner overflow 0; 936 px with a 130-px footer at y≈812), and the outer ScrollView scrolls 344 px on a 320×640 screen. So Posebni datumi and "Dodaj izuzetak" are reachable, nothing sits at y≈650, and the severity is minor, not major.
verdict.fix:
Keep the direction of the proposed fix (mirror profil/dostupnost.tsx:58), but correct the problem text: content is not unreachable. The real defects are the raw 650, the inert nested ScrollView, the doubled 20+20 gutter, and a save footer that is not pinned (it appears off-screen at y≈812 in a 560-px viewport after a change at the top).

Fix:
- Give WorkerProfileFrame an optional `scroll={false}`. With it, children render in a flex:1 View instead of the ScrollView. The default stays unchanged for /profil/radnik and /profil/lokacija, and the panel keeps the same title, "Nazad" label and keyboard-aware footer as the other razgovor panels. CalendarScreen with scroll={false} also works, but it changes the header.
- Render `<AvailabilityForm availability={data.candidate.availability} busy={editor.busy} uncertain={editor.uncertain} candidateMode onSave={…unchanged enabled + patch(workerAvailabilityPatch(…)) guard…}/>` as the frame's direct flex child, and delete the minHeight:650 View.
- Pass `footer={<>{editor.error?<T accessibilityRole="alert" tone="danger">{editor.error}</T>:null}<V2Action label="Proveri stanje razgovora" onPress={refresh} disabled={editor.busy}/></>}`. The form's uncertain-state reason (AvailabilityForm.tsx:432-433) names this check, so it must stay reachable. It is a white secondary, so it adds no second filled primary.
- Optionally show that footer only when `editor.error || editor.uncertain`, as the chat does at razgovor.tsx:244. On a 320×640 screen the list then keeps about 400 px instead of 327 px while the form's own footer is up.

Checked with the same Yoga harness: the fixed tree has one bounded scroll container (806 px of content in a 327–487 px viewport), the form's footer sits right above the frame footer at the screen foot, and the text column is 280 px at 320 dp.

No guard, server call, recovery or test intent changes: worker-ai-conversation-recovery.test.tsx mocks WorkerProfileFrame as `({children})=>children` and never opens this panel, and availability-step10.test.tsx:441 and w02-calendar-native.test.tsx:125 render AvailabilityForm directly.

verdict.evidence: The defect is real and the file is in scope. src/ui/product/ProductDetails.tsx:226 applies `disabled && s.footerDisabled`, which is `{ opacity: 0.45 }` at :333, on top of `brandAction`. In the current code the footer is disabled only while `busy`: NeedPresentation.tsx:197-199, where the label becomes 'Radnja je u toku…' and the footer sits on a white `surface` at :218, and PublicNeedPresentation.tsx:130/133/139. The result is a white label on a (143,190,175) blend: 2.07:1 with offscreen compositing, and 1.42:1 with React Native Android's default per-element alpha (needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing is false). DetailLink at :150 uses `s.disabled` = `{ opacity: 0.5 }` (:312), which drops its ink label to 3.1:1. It is disabled through TaskQaEntry.tsx:8 by prilike/[id].tsx:150 (`busy`) and pregled.tsx:205 (`!canAct()`, which includes `editor.uncertain`, so the fade can last). Both break the system rule stated in V2Action.tsx:24/58-60/147 and enforced by action-states.test.tsx:43-49 ('muted ink on the quiet wash, never a faded ghost', opacity 1). The same screen already draws `disabled={busy}` that way through V2Action at PublicNeedPresentation.tsx:87/136/143. No test depends on the faded look: pkg011-slice4:116-125 checks only `disabled === true` and that the arrow is gone, and every `brand()` check renders with busy=false. FactArt already takes `muted` (FactArt.tsx:125). The proposed muted-on-wash colours give 5.04:1. The fix changes no guard, callback, accessibilityState or copy.
verdict.fix:
The proposed fix is correct. Exact change in src/ui/product/ProductDetails.tsx:

(1) Line 333: `footerDisabled: { backgroundColor: sys.color.wash, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: sys.color.line }`. This is V2Action's `restingFilled`. It keeps its place after `brandAction` in the style array at :226, so it overrides `brandAction`'s `borderWidth: 0`. The 54 px minHeight is unchanged.

(2) Add `footerTextDisabled: { color: sys.color.muted }`. At :227 draw `<T variant="action" style={[s.footerText, disabled && s.footerTextDisabled]}>`.

(3) DetailLink:
- delete `s.disabled` (:312) and its use at :150;
- draw `<FactArt kind={art} size={28} muted={disabled} />`;
- give the label `style={disabled ? s.mutedInk : s.ink}` with `mutedInk: { color: sys.color.muted }`.

The caret and detail line are already muted. If a future caller disables a row that has `trailing`, mute the trailing element too. Today the only row with `trailing` (NeedPresentation:167) is never disabled.

Keep `disabled`, `accessibilityState`, `haptic`, the hidden arrow and every callback unchanged.

findings.rule: One time format (vreme()/civilClock): clock to the minute, seconds never
findings.problem: The weekly rows of the AI worker-profile review (WorkerAiReviewDetails, the frozen review the worker accepts) print `${r.startTime}–${r.endTime}` raw. The rules come through normalizeWorkerAvailability (src/lib/workerAvailability.ts:25), which always writes HH:MM:SS. The review therefore reads '09:00:00–17:00:00', and a day end reads '24:00:00'. AvailabilityForm shows the same rules as '09:00–17:00' through civilClock.
findings.fix: Import civilClock from '../calendar/calendarPresentation' and write `${civilClock(r.startTime)}–${civilClock(r.endTime)}`, the same shape as AvailabilityForm's clocks(). Only the display changes; the stored rule stays exact.

verdict.evidence: The defect is real. src/ui/workerProfile/WorkerAiPresentation.tsx:46 prints `${r.startTime}–${r.endTime}` as raw strings. Every review reaches it through decodeWorkerAiReview → decodeWorkerAiProfile → normalizeWorkerAvailability (src/data/workerAiClientService.ts:60,90; src/lib/workerAvailability.ts:25). That normalizer always writes HH:MM:SS, and the server also returns `start_time::text` from a Postgres `time` column. A scratch Jest render through the real decoder showed "09:00:00–17:00:00 · od 24. sep" and "22:00:00–24:00:00" on the production screen (src/app/(app)/profil/razgovor.tsx:201). The existing test (src/ui/workerProfile/__tests__/worker-ai-review.test.tsx:25) misses this because it builds the review with '08:00' directly and never goes through the decoder, even though it asserts no HH:MM:SS. The file is production code in scope: not auth/entry, not a test, not a gallery. The fix changes display text only. It leaves the save guard alone: displayedContentDigest is computed by the server and only echoed back (workerAiClientService.ts:162). It matches AvailabilityForm's clocks() (src/ui/calendar/AvailabilityForm.tsx:26). With the fix applied to a scratch copy, the decoded review renders "09:00–17:00" and "22:00–24:00" while the stored rule stays HH:MM:SS, and all 6 existing tests still pass. The repo was not modified.
verdict.fix: Keep the proposed fix. In src/ui/workerProfile/WorkerAiPresentation.tsx, extend the existing import on line 9 to `import { civilClock, civilDay, weekdays } from '../calendar/calendarPresentation';`. On line 46 write `${civilClock(r.startTime)}–${civilClock(r.endTime)} · od ...`, leaving the rest of the template unchanged. Recommended in addition, since it strengthens the test's own "no seconds" intent: in src/ui/workerProfile/__tests__/worker-ai-review.test.tsx, change the fixture times to the decoded shape ('08:00:00'/'16:00:00' at lines 25, 59 and 68), or feed the review through decodeWorkerAiReview. Then the existing assertions `toContain('08:00–16:00 · od 24. sep')` and `not.toMatch(/\d\d:\d\d:\d\d/)` fail before the fix and pass after it. One accepted edge case: civilClock shows minutes only, so a rule stored with non-zero seconds (the server allows it, w02 migration line 148) would show as its minute. This is the same documented trade-off AvailabilityForm already makes (calendarPresentation.ts:65-69) and follows the owner rule "seconds never".

The errors go through `ErrorMessage` (line 95, rendered at 507). On Android, RN only sets a roleDescription for alert (ReactAccessibilityDelegate) and iOS has no alert trait. So after the confirm sheet closes, the outcome of the one command that forms a Dogovor is silent: only a haptic and a relabelled footer button.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` to the texts at 500 and 506 and to `ErrorMessage` (line 95). For iOS, also call `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility('Dogovor je sklopljen.')` when `confirmed` turns true, as PushPreferences.tsx:366-367 does for its saved line.

verdict.evidence: At ecb0f13, src/ui/v2/ApplicationSelectionPresentation.tsx:95, :500 and :506 give `T` only `accessibilityRole="alert"`, and `T` passes it straight to RN Text (src/ui/Text.tsx:49-59). RN 0.86.3 turns that role on Android into only a roleDescription (node_modules/react-native/ReactAndroid/src/main/java/com/facebook/react/uimanager/ReactAccessibilityDelegate.kt:677-678) and on iOS into no trait at all (node_modules/react-native/ReactCommon/react/renderer/components/view/accessibilityPropsConversions.h:108, React/Views/RCTViewManager.m:31). Nothing else speaks the outcome either: SuccessMark is hidden from accessibility (src/ui/system/SuccessMark.tsx:39), ConfirmSheet says it never reports the outcome (src/ui/system/ConfirmSheet.tsx:24-25), and the route src/app/(app)/potrebe/[id]/kandidati.tsx never calls AccessibilityInfo. So the Dogovor outcome and the choose and viewed-mark errors are silent. The repo already admits this at src/ui/calendar/AvailabilityForm.tsx:345: "a role alone is not read on Android". The defect is unchanged at HEAD b4531ef (lines :70, :319, :325).
verdict.fix:
Keep `accessibilityRole="alert"` everywhere. src/ui/__tests__/screen-titles-announce-themselves.test.ts:55-66 requires a role on every `variant="title"`, and its stated intent (:15-16) is that "Dogovor je sklopljen." is announced when it appears. Then, without touching any guard:

(1) Add `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` to the T inside ErrorMessage (ecb0f13 :95; HEAD :70). This also covers the IntervalEditor error (:128) and the composer error (:216).

(2) Add `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` to "Dogovor je sklopljen." (:506; HEAD :325). For iOS, which ignores live regions, add `useEffect(() => { if (confirmed && !confirmedAtMount && Platform.OS === 'ios') AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility('Dogovor je sklopljen.'); }, [confirmed, confirmedAtMount])`. The `!confirmedAtMount` gate is the same freshness check SuccessMark already uses (:505), so a sheet reopened on a Dogovor that already exists (back from the safety screen, :502-504) does not announce again. Add AccessibilityInfo to the existing react-native import; Platform is already imported. Optionally, ErrorMessage can make the same iOS-only announcement for a new error, because the proposed fix leaves errors silent on iOS.

(3) Do NOT add a live region to the pending block (:500; HEAD :319). It appears the moment the command starts: useOwnedEditor.ts:89-92 sets busy and runs the command, which sets session.pending before its first await (kandidati.tsx:79-84). At that moment the ConfirmSheet is still open and busy (ConfirmSheet.tsx:57-61), and its title is the same CHOICE_TITLE (:456). A live region there would only repeat the question the person just confirmed, a moment before "Dogovor je sklopljen.". The block is context for a retry, not an outcome; a failed choice is already announced by the error line.

Check on the emulator with TalkBack that the confirmed line is spoken, because it appears while the ConfirmSheet's own Modal window is still closing over it. If it is not spoken, use the AvailabilityForm.tsx:342-346 pattern instead: announce on every platform when freshly confirmed, and drop the live region from that line so Android does not say it twice.

verdict.fix: The direction is right and respects the owner rules (no visual, copy, guard, server call, revision or test-intent change; only built-in RN AccessibilityInfo, no new dependency). Two refinements. (1) The error at [id].tsx:418: keep `accessibilityRole="alert"`, the words and the "Osveži status Dogovora" recovery as they are. The note mounts together with its text at the bottom of the scroll, usually off-screen after a footer command, so a live region on that freshly mounted note or Text may not be spoken by TalkBack. Two reliable options: put `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` on an always-mounted wrapper around the error slot, or say each new error once with `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility(workspace.error)` from an effect placed before the early returns at :193, gated on the Dogovor being shown so the load-error status at :58 is not said twice. On iOS the announcement is required either way (PushPreferences.tsx:365-367 pattern). (2) Success: give NextStepCard's title T (AgreementWorkspace.tsx:99) `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`. It stays mounted while its text changes ('Čeka se potvrda druge strane' / 'Dogovor je završen'), so TalkBack speaks it. iOS ignores live regions, so also announce a changed title once after mount, never on first render (the useAnnouncedReason pattern in V2Action.tsx:111-117). findings.rule: State change announced / focus lost when a view rebuilds
findings.problem: The irreversible 'Da, trajno zatvori nalog' is confirmed in the ConfirmSheet, then `run` in ClosureDialog.tsx clears `message` (line 82) and the view swaps from the review to the `state` branch ('Zahtev je pokrenut.'). The pressed DangerAction no longer exists, the sheet closes, and nothing is announced: the header has role header only, and the InlineNote alert appears only when there is a message. A screen reader user is not told that account closure has started (nor later that the account is 'zatvoren').
findings.fix: When `state` first appears and when it becomes CLOSED, announce the header text with `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility` and/or give this Text `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`. Also move accessibility focus to it with a ref and `AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(findNodeHandle(ref))`.

verdict.evidence: The defect is real. After a confirmed start, run() clears the message (ClosureDialog.tsx:82) and the read that finds the request sets state with an empty message (ClosureDialog.tsx:59-60). So the only thing that changes is the header at ClosurePresentation.tsx:102, which has role header and no live region. The alert InlineNote renders only when there is a message (ClosurePresentation.tsx:111). The pressed DangerAction exists only in the review branch (ClosurePresentation.tsx:202) and not in the state branch (125-155). ConfirmSheet leaves reporting the outcome to the screen that owns the command (ConfirmSheet.tsx:24-25). Nothing in src/ui/closure announces the change or moves focus. The sibling Izvoz flow does announce its outcome (ExportPresentation.tsx:115-117). The files are unchanged between ecb0f13 and HEAD.
verdict.fix:
The diagnosis is right; the mechanics need three corrections.

1. Timing. The state arrives while the ConfirmSheet is still open and busy: onConfirm returns start() (ClosureDialog.tsx:134), and the sheet closes only after that settles (ConfirmSheet.tsx:57-61). An announcement or focus request fired on the state change is spoken under the sheet and then lost when its Modal closes. Act only after the sheet is gone:
   - Pass `confirm.open` (useConfirmSheet already returns it) as an optional `sheetOpen` on ClosureModel. Optional keeps the gallery default at dizajn-privatnost.tsx:109 type-checking.
   - Wait until it is false, plus a short timeout so the Modal's window leaves first.

2. One mechanism, not live region + announce + focus together, or TalkBack reads the header two or three times.
   - In ClosureView, put the hooks before the early return at ClosurePresentation.tsx:89.
   - Keep a ref of the last header text. Seed it with the first header shown after loading, so opening the flow does not steal focus.
   - When the header changes to 'Zahtev je pokrenut.' or 'Nalog je zatvoren.' (after a confirmed start, a retry or a check) and no sheet is open, call `AccessibilityInfo.sendAccessibilityEvent(headerRef.current, 'focus')` once. This restores the focus lost with 'Pokreni zatvaranje naloga' / 'Ponovi isti zahtev za zatvaranje', and TalkBack and VoiceOver read the header once.

3. Do not use `setAccessibilityFocus(findNodeHandle(ref))`. It is @deprecated in RN 0.86 (react-native/Libraries/Components/AccessibilityInfo/AccessibilityInfo.js:448) and goes through the legacy tag path.

The ref reaches RN Text at runtime (React 19 passes ref through SettingsText to T). T's TextProps type has no `ref`, so declare it there or type T's props from ComponentProps<typeof Text>.

A lighter alternative is `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` on the header plus an iOS-only announce (the house pattern at DiscoveryPresentation.tsx:406-414). That announces the change but leaves focus lost.

No copy, guard, fence, idempotency or test intent changes. Add a ClosureDialog test: after a found start and the sheet closing, the header gets exactly one focus event (sendAccessibilityEvent is jest-mocked).

verdict.evidence:
The defect is real. At ecb0f13, `src/ui/v2/IntakePresentation.tsx:238` (line 201 at HEAD b4531ef, same code) draws `props.error` as `<T accessibilityRole="alert">` with no live region. It sits inside the shell's status View (`AiConversationShell.tsx:145`), which has no live region either. In RN 0.86.3 the "alert" role maps to `UIAccessibilityTraitNone` on iOS (`node_modules/react-native/React/Views/RCTViewManager.m:31`). On Android it only sets a role description (`ReactAccessibilityDelegate.kt:677`). Nothing in `nova.tsx` or `useOwnedEditor` announces the error. So when a send fails and `useOwnedEditor.ts:97` sets it, TalkBack and VoiceOver hear nothing. The `statusCopy` line (239) keeps the same text through the failure, so it is not re-announced either.

One detail in the report is wrong: the BLOCK safety line (223) is in the shell's `actions` slot (`AiConversationShell.tsx:146`), not the status slot. That slot has no live region either, so the conclusion still holds.

The file is in scope: production AI intake, not locked entry/auth, not a test, not the gallery.

1. Add `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` to the error Text (ecb0f13 :238 / HEAD :201) and to the BLOCK safety Text (ecb0f13 :223 / HEAD :186). This is the Android route. It matches the `statusCopy` line next to it and V2Action.tsx:87.

findings.problem: `Note` renders `message` and `notice` with role alert only. `message` includes the validation 'Unesi celu pozitivnu cenu u RSD i ceo broj ljudi.' that moje-prijave.tsx sets when 'Sačuvaj izmenjenu prijavu' is pressed. verdict.evidence: The defect is real and in scope. MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:44 and :141 give the list-header lines only accessibilityRole="alert", which RN 0.86 turns into a role description on Android (ReactAccessibilityDelegate.kt:677-678) and into UIAccessibilityTraitNone on iOS (RCTViewManager.m:31). So the validation that moje-prijave.tsx:174 sets from the save button at MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:89, and the outcomes (moje-prijave.tsx:110, and editor.error via :211), appear in the header at MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:140-144 and are never announced. No test pins these roles; the tests only check text.
verdict.fix:
Keep the finding, but the Android part of the proposed fix would not fire. It puts the live region on the Note's <T> and the <T> at line 141, which are leaf texts that mount together with their words. RN Fabric applies a Text's props and words before inserting it (ViewManager.java:228-233). From Android 13, TextView ignores the identical re-set after insertion (the textOrSpanChanged check). The leaf's layout change then only reaches the live regions of its ancestors, and TalkBack speaks a content change only when the event's source is itself a live region (EventTypeWindowContentChangedFeedbackRule). A live-region parent, however, sends its own event when the child is laid out (ViewGroup.notifySubtreeAccessibilityStateChanged).

Corrected fix:
(1) Put accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" on Note's tinted inset container View at line 44, not on its <T>. InlineNote.tsx:27-28 already uses this pattern. The container has a background, so Fabric keeps it as a native view.
(2) At line 141, wrap only the two sentences ("Ova prijava trenutno nije dostupna" and "Osveži spisak…") in a View with accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" and collapsable={false}. Fabric flattens a View without a background, and a live region alone does not stop that. Leave the "Osveži prijave" button outside the wrapper so its label is not read with the sentence.
(3) Keep accessibilityRole="alert" on the warn Note and on line 141. Dropping it on the muted notice is optional; it changes nothing that is spoken.
(4) iOS ignores live regions, so announce each newly shown sentence once with AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility behind Platform.OS === 'ios', as PushPreferences.tsx:365-367 does. This covers message, notice and the missing-application sentence. Call it from an effect keyed on the text, and only while the header is drawn (!loading && !unavailable), because otherwise message is the StateView body.

No copy, route, guard, server call or test intent changes, and no new dependency.

findings.rule: Missing accessibilityState.expanded / focus lost when a view rebuilds
findings.problem: The foot 'Pregledaj izmene zadatka' opens the review under the card (caret down), but it has no `expanded` state. Pressing it makes `applicationFoot(row, expanded)` return null (line 99), so the focused Press unmounts while the review mounts below. TalkBack focus is lost and nothing says that 'Aktuelni uslovi' opened.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityState={{ disabled, expanded: false }}` to the review foot. After expanding, move accessibility focus to the review header 'Aktuelni uslovi' (MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:76) with a ref and `AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(findNodeHandle(ref))`. Alternatively, keep the foot mounted as a toggle with `expanded: true`.

verdict.evidence: The defect is real and in scope: at src/ui/v2/ApplicationFace.tsx:203-204 the review foot only has `accessibilityState={{ disabled }}`, and pressing it runs moje-prijave.tsx:219 (session.expanded = id), which passes expanded=true at MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:101, so applicationFoot returns null at ApplicationFace.tsx:99 and the focused Press unmounts, while the review mounts at MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:75-76 as a plain View with no live region and no focus call (no setAccessibilityFocus or sendAccessibilityEvent exists anywhere in src at ecb0f13).
verdict.fix:
Keep the main fix, with four corrections, and drop the alternative.
(1) Put `expanded: false` on the review foot only (`action === 'review'`). The withdraw foot must keep exactly `{ disabled }`, because application-face.test.tsx:135 checks `toEqual({ disabled: true })`. With expanded:false, RN 0.86 on Android adds ACTION_EXPAND to the node (ReactAccessibilityDelegate.kt:74-79). That action does nothing unless it is declared. So also add `accessibilityActions={[{ name: 'expand' }]}` and `onAccessibilityAction={e => { if (e.nativeEvent.actionName === 'expand' && !disabled) onFoot(); }}`. Otherwise TalkBack's "Expand" (Proširi) action is a dead button.
(2) Move focus with `AccessibilityInfo.sendAccessibilityEvent(headerRef.current, 'focus')`, not with `setAccessibilityFocus(findNodeHandle(ref))`, which is `@deprecated` in RN 0.86.3 (AccessibilityInfo.js:448). Give the "Aktuelni uslovi" header (MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:76) a ref. T spreads `...rest` into RNText, so under React 19 a `ref` prop reaches the host Text, but T's Props type (Text.tsx:37) needs `ref?: Ref<Text>`. Alternatively, wrap the header in a View that has the ref.
(3) Send the focus only once, after the review mounts because the person pressed the foot. For example: the presentation wraps onReview and records `focusNext = p.prijavaId`, still calling the route's guarded `props.onReview(p)` unchanged. A `useEffect` keyed on `expandedRow?.prijavaId` then sends the focus on the next frame and clears `focusNext`. Do not send it on every mount: the FlatList (windowSize 7) can remount the expanded cell while the person scrolls, which would steal focus. The notification landing at moje-prijave.tsx:126 may use the same one-shot.
(4) Optionally, mirror this for "Zatvori pregled izmena" (MyApplicationsPresentation.tsx:96). That button also unmounts itself, so focus should return to the re-drawn foot.
Drop the alternative "keep the foot mounted as a toggle with expanded: true". It contradicts the deliberate rule at ApplicationFace.tsx:97-99: the foot is not drawn twice while the review, which has its own close, is open. It would also break the intent of src/data/__tests__/application-face.test.tsx:88 and :142 (review open → no foot; `applicationFoot(row, true)` is null).
No new copy, motion or dependency is needed, and no guard, revision or idempotency path changes.

findings.problem: The reason for a grey button reaches assistive technology only as `accessibilityHint` (71). verdict.evidence: The defect is real and in scope. src/ui/v2/V2Action.tsx:71 gives the reason to assistive technology only as `accessibilityHint`, which RN 0.86.3 on Android turns into `tooltipText` (node_modules/react-native/ReactAndroid/.../uimanager/ReactAccessibilityDelegate.kt:87-88). The drawn line is hidden at :86, and `useAnnouncedReason` starts `spoken` with the first reason (:112), so that reason is never announced. The repo's own round-5c note (src/ui/calendar/AvailabilityForm.tsx:73-75; docs/implementation/design-system/cloud-handoff/round5b/kalendar-verify-iskustvo.md:17) records that a hint goes unheard when hints are off. The same pattern is at src/ui/aiFirst/AiConversationShell.tsx:158/173 and src/ui/AgreementChat.tsx:248, which has no visible line at all.
verdict.fix:
The proposed `accessibilityValue={why ? { text: why } : undefined}` breaks on Android when the reason clears:
- Pressable always sends `{max, min, now, text}` (Libraries/Components/Pressable/Pressable.js:238-243).
- JSI drops the undefined `text` (ReactCommon/jsi/jsi/JSIDynamic.cpp:186), so the view receives `{}`.
- `BaseViewManager.setAccessibilityValue` rebuilds contentDescription only when the map has a `text` key (BaseViewManager.java:466).
- The result: the enabled button keeps saying the old reason. The "keep the hint" option also says the reason twice when hints are on.

Corrected fix: put the reason in the accessible name, because `setAccessibilityLabel` always rebuilds contentDescription (BaseViewManager.java:331-333).
- In V2Action: `const name = accessibilityLabel ?? label;` then `accessibilityLabel={why ? `${name}. ${why}` : name}`, and drop `accessibilityHint`. Keep line 86 hidden so the reason is said once, and keep `useAnnouncedReason` for a reason that appears later.
- AiConversationShell.tsx:172-173: `const sendLabel = p.pending ? 'Ponovi istu poruku' : 'Pošalji poruku'` and `accessibilityLabel={sendReason ? `${sendLabel}. ${sendReason}` : sendLabel}`, with no hint.
- AgreementChat.tsx:247-248: `accessibilityLabel={forcedWhy ? `Fotografije uz poruku. ${forcedWhy}` : 'Fotografije uz poruku'}`, with no hint.

Nothing visual changes and no guard or server call is touched. The tests that read the hint (application-composer-read.test.tsx:130-131, ai-conversation-layout.test.tsx:140-151, agreement-chat-ui.test.tsx:295-301) need to find the button by label prefix or testID and assert the reason in the label with no hint. Their intent stays the same: the reason is spoken once while the button is grey and is gone when the button is live.

findings.rule: Back that lands somewhere unexpected
findings.problem: After a confirmed choice, 'Otvori Dogovor' calls router.replace('/dogovor/[id]') from inside the (app) Tabs (same at line 142 for an offer that was already SELECTED). '/dogovor/[id]' is a route of the ROOT Stack, so expo-router's getNavigateAction diverges at the root and dispatches REPLACE to the root stack, whose StackRouter replaces the route at state.index, i.e. the whole '(app)' tab navigator. On the common paths (Početna 'Čeka te' / Moji zadaci / own task -> Prijave) the root stack becomes [dogovor/[id]] alone: Android Back from the freshly formed Dogovor exits the app, and the arrow (backToAgreements -> canGoBack() false -> replace('/dogovori')) builds a new tab shell whose history is only [dogovori], so the next Back exits the app too. Početna, the task and the whole tab history are gone.
findings.fix: Do not replace across navigators. Close the offer sheet first (navigate from the sheet's onClose, as ActionSheet runs an action only once its sheet is gone) and then router.push({ pathname: '/dogovor/[id]', params: { id } }) so the (app) shell stays under the Dogovor; keep session.navigated and every guard. Update the three `mockRouter.replace` expectations for 'Otvori Dogovor' in src/data/__tests__/application-selection-native.test.tsx to push (same intent: the choice opens the Dogovor).

verdict.evidence: The bug is real. At src/app/(app)/potrebe/[id]/kandidati.tsx:142 and :155, `router.replace` is called for `/dogovor/[id]`, which is registered on the root Stack (src/app/_layout.tsx:138). expo-router's findDivergentState (node_modules/expo-router/build/global-state/stateUtils.js:62) sees the paths split at that root Stack. It then sends REPLACE with no source, and StackRouter.js:155-173 swaps out the route at state.index, which is the whole `(app)` tab shell. I checked this on the real Expo Router runtime with the real (app) Tabs layout, in a throwaway copy of ecb0f13. From Početna→Kandidati or task→Kandidati, the root stack went from [(app)] to [dogovor/[id]] and canGoBack() was false. The Dogovor arrow (dogovor/[id].tsx:54, replace('/dogovori')) then left [(app)] with tab history ['dogovori'] and canGoBack false, so the next Back exits the app. With push the stack is [(app), dogovor/[id]], the tab history stays whole, and Back returns to Kandidati and then to Početna or the task. The file is in scope: not an entry/auth file, a test or a gallery.
verdict.fix:
The proposed fix is right; add one test change. At kandidati.tsx:142 and :155, open the Dogovor with `router.push({ pathname: '/dogovor/[id]', params: { id } })` (or `router.navigate`, which every other Dogovor entry uses: dogovori.tsx:70, index.tsx:50, prilike/[id].tsx:169) and not with replace. Keep `current()`, `session.navigated` and the receipt checks exactly as they are.

Closing the offer sheet first is optional polish that follows the ActionSheet pattern (ActionSheet.tsx:36). If you do it, the sheet's onClose is currently `back`, which leaves Kandidati once `pending` is set. So route the close through a one-time "open this Dogovor" intent that pushes, instead of calling back().

A plain push already works:
- When the screen loses focus, useOwnedEditor clears `data`, so the sheet's Modal unmounts.
- When the screen comes back into focus, `read()` resets `session.navigated`, so nothing is left dead.
- The confirmed sheet showing again on return matches the existing round trip from the safety screen.

Tests in src/data/__tests__/application-selection-native.test.tsx:
- Change the three `mockRouter.replace` expectations at lines 295, 377 and 460 to `mockRouter.push`.
- Also add `expect(mockRouter.push).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` at line 383. Otherwise "never opens its Agreement" passes without checking anything.

verdict.evidence:
The defect is real and in scope. At src/ui/agreements/AgreementCompletionReview.tsx:19 (identical at ecb0f13 and HEAD b4531ef) the review is a hand-made `<Modal visible presentationStyle="pageSheet">`. `presentationStyle` only works on iOS, so on Android it opens as a full-screen page. It has its own ProductHeader (L21), a single footer V2Action (L48-50) and no quiet cancel. USKOCI_MASTER_PLAN_DIZAJNA.md:27 and :35 list "pregled završetka" among the hand-made Modals the Sheet family replaces, and the offer review already made this exact move (ApplicationComposerPresentation.tsx:355-359, following r6-specs/prijava.spec.json). I tested it in an isolated scratch copy, leaving the repository untouched. A ProductSheet version kept all 110 tests of pkg011-agreement-workspace and agreement-screen-recovery passing, and tsc showed no errors in the changed component or the outputs fixture. Only three display checks had to change: Modal.animationType became the sheet's animateOnMount, and "Nazad na Dogovor" became "Odustani" in two places. Every guard check stayed as it was: stale confirm and back, blur, new read, account change, double submit, unknown result and native Back. - Its title "Pregled završetka" names the step and would sit above a second heading. The app's confirm sheets use the question as the title (e.g. "Povući prijavu?", moje-prijave.tsx:192).
verdict.fix:
Keep the props `{agreement, worker, confirm, back}`. Then src/app/dogovor/[id].tsx (reviewingCompletion, confirmCompletionReview, dismissCompletionReview) and the type-checked outputs/native-product-review-20260922/review.tsx stay unchanged. The old web preview's done-* scenes will stop rendering, as its Discovery scene already did.

Render it as `<ProductSheet title={worker ? 'Javi da je posao gotov' : 'Potvrdi obavljen posao'} closeButton={false} reduced={useSystemReducedMotion()} backdropHint="Vraća na Dogovor bez potvrde." onClose={back}>`. The role question becomes the one green title instead of "Pregled završetka".

Content (children function):

verdict.evidence: razgovor.tsx:140 returns early whenever editor.busy is true. useOwnedEditor.ts:89-106 keeps busy true for the whole editor.save, and in send (razgovor.tsx:102-117) that covers journal.save, then api.send (55 s timeout, workerAiClientService.ts:170), then read(). No test depends on the fence (worker-ai-conversation-recovery.test.tsx never presses back), and the file is not a locked entry/auth file, a test or a gallery.

Take the proposal's first option: in razgovor.tsx:140, drop `editor.busy` from back() and keep `!current()`, as nova.tsx:123-125 does. Leaving already runs this screen's focus cleanup, which aborts and clears the stream (:46-48). It also runs useOwnedEditor's cleanup, which retires the scope and clears busy. On return, read() recovers the turn by the same clientRequestId (:60-78). Android Back already takes exactly this path today, so no guard, recovery, idempotency key or server call changes.

Also fix the sub-panel branch. There, back() only returns to the chat. Letting it run while busy has one catch: an in-flight review() calls setPanel('review') at :155 and would reopen the review after the person went back. Choose one:
- (a) Allow it, and let review() set the 'review' panel only if the panel is unchanged since the call started (keep a panel ref).

findings.rule: disabled button without a reason

That error and its button sit in a WorkspaceNote at the END of the ScrollView (line 418), usually off screen, while the pinned footer shows a grey primary with no reason. In dogovor/[id].tsx set loading while the completion command it started runs (workspace.busy) instead of the label swap, and reason = 'Najpre osveži status Dogovora.' when workspace.error || workspace.uncertain (the fresh-read condition the save requires). No guard changes.

verdict.evidence: The defect is real. src/app/dogovor/[id].tsx:173 and :291-293 grey out the pinned brand action whenever workspace.error, uncertain or busy is set, and the only explanation, with the only 'Osveži status Dogovora', is drawn at the end of the ScrollView (:418-419). WorkspaceFooter (src/ui/agreements/AgreementWorkspace.tsx:126-128) passes neither `reason` nor `loading` to V2Action, although V2Action accepts both (src/ui/v2/V2Action.tsx:38-51), so a write shows 'Čuvamo promenu…' (:280) on a grey button instead of the spinner. However, the proposed `loading = workspace.busy` is wrong: workspace.busy is also set by mutate (:229-238, 'Podeli svoj broj') and by reportProblem (:209-228), so 'Potvrdi završetak' would spin while a problem report is being saved. That breaks V2Action's rule that loading means 'The write this action started is in flight' (V2Action.tsx:47) and the app's existing pattern `publishWorking = editor.busy && publishing` (src/app/(app)/pregled-zadatka.tsx:280-282).
verdict.fix:
1) src/ui/agreements/AgreementWorkspace.tsx:126 — extend WorkspaceFooter's `brand` type with `loading?: boolean; reason?: string | null` and pass both to V2Action (`loading={brand.loading} reason={brand.reason}`). brandAction has no placement keys, so the reason column keeps the green surface on the Press, and the dizajn-dogovori gallery call still compiles.
2) src/app/dogovor/[id].tsx — track the completion's own write, as pregled-zadatka.tsx:71/157-164 does. Add `const [completing, setCompleting] = useState(false)`. Inside complete(), after its existing guard, set it as the first line of the workspace.save callback (with a `started` flag) and clear it in a `finally` around `await workspace.save(...)`. This is display state only: the order of `enabled`, canComplete, save and readback does not change.
3) Drop the label swap: `completeLabel = worker ? 'Posao je gotov' : 'Potvrdi završetak'`. Compute `const brandReason = workspace.loading ? 'Učitavamo Dogovor…' : workspace.error || workspace.uncertain ? 'Najpre osveži status Dogovora.' : workspace.busy && !completing ? 'Čuvamo promenu…' : null`. The loading branch must come first: refresh clears `error` at its start but keeps `uncertain` until a successful read (useOwnedEditor.ts:33-34,44). Without it, the proposed reason would say 'refresh first' while that refresh is already running and the note has disappeared.
4) Completion brand: `{ label: completeLabel, disabled: !enabled, loading: workspace.busy && completing, reason: brandReason }`. For 'Odgovori na predlog' and 'Oceni saradnju', add `reason: brandReason`. Keep `disabled: !enabled` exactly as it is, and leave 'Otvori poruke' unchanged.
5) Move the existing `workspace.error` WorkspaceNote from after problemPanel (:418-419) to directly under NextStepCard, with the same text and the single 'Osveži status Dogovora'. Then the refresh the reason points to is on screen, and it also explains why the WorkspaceRows are faded to 0.5.

findings.problem: The conversation's '···' stays pressable while a turn runs, but its rows 'Osveži razgovor' (readbackDisabled), 'Novi Zadatak' (newTaskDisabled) and 'Napusti razgovor' (abandonDisabled, whose subtitle only states the consequence) are drawn grey with no reason. findings.fix: Have nova.tsx compute one reason ('Dostupno kad se završi slanje.' while radi, 'Dostupno kad se razgovor učita.' while loading, 'Prvo proveri ishod.' when uncertain or a turn is pending) and pass it as each disabled row's subtitle (for the abandon row, prepend it to the existing consequence line).

findings.rule: honest error state
findings.problem: On a group Dogovor the entry reads the group context; when that read fails (!result.ok, e.g. offline) or rejects (no .catch), the component renders null: the 'Grupni razgovor' button and the 'otvara se kada…' line both vanish with no error and no retry, so the person cannot tell a missing group from a failed read.
findings.fix: Keep a 'failed' state: on !result.ok or a rejection (add .catch) render a quiet line 'Grupni razgovor trenutno nije učitan.' with a quiet 'Pokušaj ponovo' that bumps `epoch` (the effect's existing re-read trigger).

findings.rule: honest empty/error state (way forward)
findings.problem: When the task is missing (closed, or no longer visible to this account) the card says 'Možda je zatvoren ili više nije dostupan tvom nalogu. Vrati se na Zadatke.', but the only button is 'Pokušaj ponovo', which re-reads the same missing task; with no id there is no button at all. The footer (and its 'Drugi zadaci') is not drawn in this state, so the way forward the copy names is not offered.
findings.fix: In the missing (non-error) state draw the route's onOtherTasks as the primary 'Drugi zadaci' (router.navigate('/zadaci') behind the existing navigate fence) and keep 'Pokušaj ponovo' as the quiet action (or only for the error state).

findings.rule: honest empty state
findings.problem: hasFilter includes `view.section !== 'active'`, so an empty Nacrti or Istorija tab with no search and no filter says 'Nema zadataka u ovom prikazu / Promeni pretragu ili poništi filtere.' with 'Poništi filtere' — there is no search or filter to clear; the button only jumps back to Aktivni.
findings.fix: Use a filter test without the section (`!!view.query || view.price !== 'all' || view.attention`) for that state; an empty section on its own gets its own words ('Nema nacrta' / 'Još nema završenih zadataka') with a quiet 'Prikaži aktivne' (change({ section: 'active' })).

findings.rule: honest loading state
findings.problem: The route's useOwnedEditor keeps the rows during a re-read (useOwnedEditor.ts:35-39: emptying the screen on 'Osveži' 'reads as having deleted the thing you were looking at'), but this presentation throws them away whenever loading is true: data={props.loading || props.unavailable ? [] : visible}, the tab row is hidden (line 125) and the skeleton replaces the list, while RefreshControl refreshing={props.loading} (line 139) spins at the same time. Every pull, 'Proveri sačuvano stanje' and 'Osveži prijave' empties Moje prijave and rebuilds it; the first read shows two loading indicators.
findings.fix: Show the skeleton only when there are no rows yet (props.loading && !props.rows.length); otherwise keep the list and tabs on screen and let RefreshControl (refreshing only for a user-asked re-read) say it is reading.

findings.rule: loading state / disabled button without a reason
findings.problem: 'Sačuvaj izmenjenu prijavu', 'Zadrži prijavu', 'Izmeni prijavu' and 'Povuci izmenjenu prijavu' (lines 89-94) all get disabled={busy || pending || editingLoading} and none gets `loading`: after a press every decision turns grey with no spinner on the pressed one, and the only progress line ('Čekamo potvrdu radnje…') is in the list header, which is off screen when the expanded card is lower in the list.
findings.fix: Pass which decision is running (from the route's pending intent) and give that button loading={busy}; give the others a reason ('Čekamo potvrdu prethodne radnje.') while busy or pending.

findings.rule: confirmation bypasses ConfirmSheet / loading state
findings.problem: 'Zatvori obrađeni predmet' closes the case on the first tap (controller.submit('CLOSE')) with no question, unlike every other terminal command in the app; 'Preuzmi predmet' (176) and 'Označi prikazane događaje kao pročitane' (171) likewise show no loading of their own — every control just turns grey while phase is SENDING.
findings.fix: Ask 'Zatvoriti predmet?' through useConfirmSheet before submit('CLOSE') (onConfirm returns the submit promise), and pass loading={state.phase === 'SENDING' && state.pending?.kind === 'CLOSE'} (and 'CLAIM' / command === 'MARK' for the other two) to the pressed SettingsAction.

findings.rule: disabled button without a reason
findings.problem: The Dogovor's send button is disabled={!canSend} with no accessibilityHint and no visible reason while the outbox is still loading, photos are loading/being prepared, or a selection is not ready; a screen reader hears only 'Pošalji poruku, onemogućeno'. The AI composer (sendReason) and the support composer (why) both say why their send is grey.
findings.fix: Compute a reason as SupportComposer does ('Učitavamo sačuvane poruke…' while !ready, 'Fotografije se još pripremaju.' while photos load/busy, the existing sentence when !writable, the length line when over 2.000) and pass it as the send's accessibilityHint; show it as a muted line above the pill when the draft is not empty.

findings.rule: Back that lands somewhere unexpected
findings.problem: A tapped notification always router.push('/obavestenja'). When the Inbox is already the screen on show (a banner tapped while reading it), a second Inbox is stacked on the first, and Back lands on the same Inbox again.
findings.fix: Use router.navigate('/obavestenja'): expo-router's stack NAVIGATE reuses the Inbox when it is the current route and pushes it otherwise, exactly as now. Keep the cold-start pendingRoute record and the ownership guards.

findings.rule: honest error state
findings.problem: The map's failure state always says 'Proveri vezu. Uneti podaci ostaju u obrascu.' It is also shown on the read-only maps (disabled) of the public task, the owner's task and the Dogovor, where there is no form and nothing was entered.
findings.fix: When props.disabled, say only 'Mapa nije učitana. Proveri vezu.' (keep 'Pokušaj ponovo sa mapom'); keep the form sentence for the editable picker.

findings.rule: loading state
findings.problem: 'Podeli svoj broj' / 'Opozovi deljenje broja' run mutate() with only disabled={!enabled}: during the write the pressed button just turns grey with no spinner and no change of words, like every other control; 'Pošalji prijavu problema' (327-328) swaps its label to 'Čuvamo prijavu…' on a greyed button instead of the V2Action loading state.
findings.fix: Remember which inline command started the save and pass loading={workspace.busy && started === 'phone'} (and 'problem' for the report) to the pressed V2Action, keeping every enabled/formCurrent guard.

findings.rule: disabled button without a reason
findings.problem: In the Filteri sheet 'Prikaži zadatke' is disabled whenever the list is loading or failed (draftCount === null) and says nothing about why.
findings.fix: Pass reason={loading ? 'Zadaci se još učitavaju.' : 'Zadaci nisu učitani. Pokušaj ponovo iz liste.'} while draftCount is null.

findings.rule: disabled button without a reason
findings.problem: 'Primeni rok na pregled' is disabled while the date or the time is empty, with no reason drawn or spoken.
findings.fix: Pass reason={!date || !time ? 'Izaberi datum i vreme roka.' : null} to the V2Action.

findings.rule: No motion under reduced motion; all motion reads the one store (src/ui/system/motion.ts)
findings.problem: The root Stack sets `animation: 'slide_from_right'` for every screen it owns without reading the reduced-motion store. Those screens are dogovor/[id] with its izmene/lokacija/grupa children, obavestenja and prijave. None of expo-router, @react-navigation/native-stack or react-native-screens handles reduced motion itself (their sources have no reference to it). So a person with reduce motion on still gets a full slide on every Dogovor and inbox open. Every push inside the (app) Tabs is already gated on the store (`PUSHED = reducedMotion ? { animation: 'none' } : PUSH_TRANSITION`); the root Stack is the gap.
findings.fix: In RootLayout, right after `useReducedMotionRoot(useLaunchReducedMotion())` (line 28) and before the `!isLoaded` return, read `const reduced = useReducedMotion()` from '../ui/system/motion'. The seed runs earlier in the same render, so the first frame is already correct. Then set `animation: reduced ? 'none' : 'slide_from_right'` in the Stack's screenOptions. auth and oporavak keep their explicit 'none'.

verdict.evidence: The defect is real and in scope. `src/app/_layout.tsx:130` (the same at ecb0f13 and HEAD) sets `animation: 'slide_from_right'` for the whole root Stack and never reads the store. `src/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:125-126` does gate its pushes on the store, through `useSystemReducedMotion`, which `src/hooks/useSystemReducedMotion.ts:6` re-exports from `ui/system/motion`. A grep of `node_modules/expo-router/build` (with its vendored `native-stack` fork) and of all of `react-native-screens` finds no reference to reduce motion at all. On Android, `FragmentTransactionKt.kt:31-35` plays `rns_slide_in_from_right.xml`, a `<translate>` tween at `config_mediumAnimTime`, so `dogovor/[id]`, its `grupa`, `izmene` and `lokacija` routes, and `obavestenja` (opened by `InboxBell.tsx:47` and `PushRuntime.tsx:73`) all slide with reduce motion on. One small correction: `src/app/prijave.tsx:5-8` is a retired redirect, not a real screen. No test checks the root Stack's animation, and `src/data/__tests__/system-reduced-motion-hook.test.tsx` uses its own Root, so adding the root as a store reader breaks no test's intent. Nothing locked is touched, because `auth` (`:134`) and `oporavak` (`:144`) keep their explicit `'none'`.
verdict.fix:
The proposed fix is correct. Only one precision is added: where the hook has to go.
1. Line 9 becomes `import { useReducedMotion, useReducedMotionRoot } from '../ui/system/motion';`. There is no name clash, because line 7 already imports Reanimated's hook as `useLaunchReducedMotion`.
2. Right after line 28 (`useReducedMotionRoot(useLaunchReducedMotion());`), add `const reduced = useReducedMotion();`. It must come before the `if (!isLoaded) return` at line 105, because of the Rules of Hooks. `seedReducedMotion` runs earlier in the same render and only while no reader is subscribed, so the first frame already reads the launch value.
3. Line 130 becomes `animation: reduced ? 'none' : 'slide_from_right',`.
Leave the explicit `animation: 'none'` on `auth` and `oporavak` untouched. This matches the Tabs pattern (`PUSHED = reducedMotion ? { animation: 'none' } : PUSH_TRANSITION`). RootLayout re-renders only when the setting really changes, and its effects do not depend on that value.

findings.rule: Motion only on a real state change; streamed text gets no entrance (the shell's own rule, lines 130-131); content already on screen is never re-animated
findings.problem: `seen` is filled only on the first render, so every later turn mounts with FadeInDown (line 238). At the end of each exchange the 'šalje se' pill (`sentMessage`, line 135) and the streamed answer (`streamingText`, line 138) are removed. The read-back then mounts the same two texts as new Turns, which fade in from opacity 0 and slide 8 px. The person's own words, and the answer they just watched stream, blink out and animate back in on every AI turn, in both conversations. In the intake it is worse: nova.tsx:160 clears the streamed text as soon as sendMessage resolves, before `read()` (two more round trips) lands. The answer is replaced by the typing dots and then fades back in.
findings.fix: In the shell, keep the last non-empty `p.sentMessage` and `p.streamingText` in refs. Before mapping, add to `seen` the id of any new turn whose body equals one of them (a user turn equal to the sent text, an AI turn equal to the streamed text). Only a turn that was not already shown then enters with motion. In nova.tsx, move the success-path `setStreamingText('')` to after the read settles. Keep the existing clearing on abort, failure and focus loss unchanged. It is display state only.

findings.rule: Performance: no heavy work in render (list rows, per keystroke)
findings.problem:
`zonedParts` builds a new `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { timeZone, … })` on every call. `displayDate` (line 54) calls `toLocaleDateString` with options, which builds another formatter each time. On Hermes Android each is an ICU formatter created through JNI. They run many times per row inside render:
- `needScheduleText` does 3-5 zonedParts, 2 displayDate and a `deviceZone()` constructor for every TaskCard render (TaskCard.tsx:64) and every CandidateCard that has a proposed time. That is ~40 formatters per FlatList batch while scrolling.
- `vreme()` does zonaTelefona, 2 zonedParts and a displayDate. SupportDetailScreen rebuilds its thread and re-formats every event (supportTime at lines 97/114/119) on each reply keystroke.
- `IntakePresentation.publicSummary` → `fixedRange` → `raspon` builds ~9 formatters on every AI-composer keystroke.
- `MyApplicationsPresentation.reviewOf` (needScheduleText + deviceZone) runs on every offer-edit keystroke.
- Also: `inboxRows` on each inbox page, the AgendaScreen strip (7 civilDay + weekLabel + dayHeading per day tap), AgendaRow, and AvailabilityForm windows.
findings.fix:
Cache formatters at module level:
- zonedParts: a `Map<string, Intl.DateTimeFormat>` keyed by zone. Store an entry only after a successful construction, so an invalid zone still throws exactly as today (callers rely on that).
- displayDate: one shared `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('sr-Latn-RS', { timeZone: 'UTC', day: 'numeric', month: 'short' })`. Its `.format()` gives the same text as `toLocaleDateString` with those options.
- Optionally memoize `publicSummary(conversation.facts)` in IntakePresentation with useMemo on `conversation.facts`.
No output changes.

verdict.evidence: Confirmed at ecb0f13, where calendarPresentation.ts is byte-identical to HEAD. Every zonedParts call builds a new formatter (src/ui/calendar/calendarPresentation.ts:14), and every displayDate call builds another through toLocaleDateString (:54). TaskCard.tsx:64 runs on each render of a FlatList or BottomSheetFlatList row (MarketplacePresentation.tsx:51, DiscoveryPresentation.tsx:57). Each time it calls needScheduleText, which does 3-5 zonedParts, 2 displayDate and one deviceZone constructor (needDetailPresentation.ts:28/38/42/49/78). SupportDetailScreen.tsx:97/114/119 re-runs vreme() for every event on each reply keystroke (setReply at :140); vreme() builds 4 formatters per event. In a Node check a fresh formatter cost 55 µs per call against 2-4 µs cached, with 0 output differences over 5 years of dates and 8,000 zoned instants, and an invalid zone still threw RangeError without being cached. The file is not a locked entry/auth file, a test or a gallery, so it is in scope. "major" may be too high, since the Hermes cost was not measured on a device.
verdict.fix:
Apply the proposed fix, with four refinements. Output does not change.
(1) zonedParts: add a module-level `const zoned = new Map<string, Intl.DateTimeFormat>()`. Get the formatter, or construct it and call `set` only after construction succeeds. An invalid zone then still throws each time: civilInstant keeps returning 'Proveri vremensku zonu.' (pkg003-timezone.test.ts), and the try/catch in needScheduleText, vreme, trenutak and marketplaceView keeps working. Skip the cache when `typeof timezone !== 'string'`: an undefined timeZone resolves to the phone's zone at construction, and caching it would freeze that zone. Keep formatToParts, `get` and the return shape exactly as they are.
(2) displayDate: create one `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('sr-Latn-RS', { timeZone: 'UTC', day: 'numeric', month: 'short' })` LAZILY on the first call, not at import. A formatter failure then stays inside the callers' try/catch as it does today, instead of breaking every importer of the module. Return `fmt.format(new Date(`${day}T12:00:00Z`))`. Because day and month are given, this is the same text as toLocaleDateString (ECMA-402 adds no defaults). The pinned-reference test in dogovorenoVreme.test.ts:59-64 keeps its intent.
(3) Do NOT cache deviceZone(), zonaTelefona() or `Intl.DateTimeFormat()` (the default-zone formatter): the phone's zone can change while the app runs, and dogovorenoVreme.test.ts:67-73 spies on resolvedOptions.
(4) Drop the optional useMemo of publicSummary on `conversation.facts`. Through raspon/vreme it reads `new Date()` (the current year) and the phone's zone (napomenaZone), so memoizing on facts alone could show a stale year or zone note. The formatter cache already removes the cost.
No dependency, guard, server call or text changes.

findings.rule: Performance: long lists must not re-render every row, with fresh closures, on each keystroke
findings.problem: The Dogovor conversation draws every message with `shown.map(...)` inside a plain ScrollView. Each bubble gets a new `onLongPress` closure and has `messageMoment`/`messageSpoken` recomputed. The draft lives in the outbox snapshot (`state.draft`), so every keystroke publishes a new snapshot and re-renders DogovorContent and this component. That re-renders every bubble: its Press with its animated style, both T texts, and each AuthorizedPhoto. The message read (`supabaseIzvor.poruke`) has no limit, so typing lag grows with the whole history.

findings.rule: Motion only on a real state change; nothing moves (or stays moved) under reduced motion
findings.problem: The swing's cleanup only calls `run.stop()`, which freezes the glyph at its current angle. The next effect run then returns early at line 37 (`reduced`, `count == null` or `count <= before`) without resetting it. Leaving the tab during the 620 ms swing makes `useInbox` stop its model (page → null, count undefined), so the bell on the root header stays tilted (up to −12°) until the next unread increase. Turning on reduced motion mid-swing freezes it tilted for good.
findings.fix: Reset on every stop: `return () => { run.stop(); swing.setValue(0); };`. Also call `swing.setValue(0)` on the early-return path at line 37. An interrupted swing then always ends upright, including under reduced motion.

findings.rule: Motion only on a real state change: only a genuinely new row arrives (Appear contract; InboxPresentation useArrivals: 'another filter is another list… what was there, not news')
findings.problem: `useAppear` is settled with the ids of the section-filtered `visible` list (Aktivni by default). The first switch to Nacrti or Istorija, or 'Prikaži sve moje zadatke', treats every card there as an arrival and slides it in with the stagger. Switching back and forth later is silent, so the same tap moves differently each time. AgreementCollectionPresentation.tsx:217 has the same defect for Dogovori → Istorija. The Inbox already handles filters correctly.
findings.fix: Settle with every id the screen holds (`items.map(keyOf)`). Then, on each render, call `appear.isNew(id)` for items that are not in `visible`, marking them seen as useArrivals does for other filters. Only an id that newly appears while its section is shown will animate. Make the same change at AgreementCollectionPresentation.tsx:217.

findings.rule: Motion only on a real state change; one transition per change; no fact animated on its own
findings.problem: SelectionFrame wraps its whole body in `Animated.View entering={FadeIn}`, so every mount fades the entire content in. That covers SelectionUnavailable's skeleton and error on the candidates route, and the composer with the task price. The (app) navigator is already running the push transition for the same change, so there are two animations for one change, including a block of facts fading on its own. No other detail screen does this.
findings.fix: Render a plain `<View style={s.stack}>` and drop `entering`. The push transition, already gated on the store, carries the arrival.

findings.rule: Performance: no heavy work in render
findings.problem: `draftCount` runs a full `marketplaceItems` pass (join plus `toLocaleLowerCase('sr-Latn-RS')` per task) whenever `view` changes, which means every keystroke in the search field. Its only reader is the Filteri sheet, which is closed while typing, so each keystroke filters the list twice.
findings.fix: Compute it only while the sheet is open: `useMemo(() => !filterOpen || loading || error ? null : marketplaceItems(items, { ...view, price: priceDraft, attention: attentionDraft }, true).length, [filterOpen, items, view, priceDraft, attentionDraft, loading, error])`. The button that reads it renders only inside the open sheet.

findings.rule: No motion under reduced motion (the wrapper's own contract: stand on the first frame)
findings.problem: When reduced motion turns on while an animation plays, the wrapper only flips props: autoPlay false, loop false, progress 0. lottie-react-native 7.3.8 never pauses on autoPlay false: LottieAnimationViewPropertyManager only calls playAnimation when autoPlay is true. Setting progress on a running view does not stop it either. The animation therefore plays out its current cycle and rests on its last frame, not the first. Latent: no screen uses LottieArt yet.
findings.fix: Remount on the switch with `key={still ? 'still' : 'moving'}` on LottieView. Alternatively, hold a ref and call `reset()` in an effect when `still` becomes true. Either way the first frame shows as soon as motion is reduced.

findings.rule: No motion under reduced motion
findings.problem: When `fresh`, the values start at scale 0.6 and opacity 0 regardless of `reduced`. The effect that sets them to 1 runs after the first paint, so under reduced motion the mark is invisible for a frame and then pops in. Arrive, ConfirmedCheck and FooterIn all initialise from `reduced`.
findings.fix: Use `new Animated.Value(fresh && !reduced ? 0.6 : 1)` and `new Animated.Value(fresh && !reduced ? 0 : 1)`.

findings.rule: Performance: no heavy work in render
findings.problem: WindowSheet computes `initialStart`/`initialEnd` with `zonedParts` (a new Intl.DateTimeFormat each) on every render, although they only seed useState. Every keystroke in 'Naziv izuzetka' and every picker change reruns two formatter constructions. ResponseDeadlineEditor.tsx:10 has the same pattern.
findings.fix: Use lazy initialisers, e.g. `useState(() => window ? zonedParts(new Date(window.startsAt), timezone) : { date: '', time: '' })`, and the same for the end. In ResponseDeadlineEditor use `const [initial] = useState(() => p.value ? zonedParts(new Date(p.value), p.timezone) : { date: '', time: '' })`.

findings.rule: Performance: no heavy work in render
findings.problem: `agendaCoverage` and `withoutExactTerm` each rebuild a lower-cased Set of the week's events and walk every Dogovor on every render, i.e. every day tap in the strip. The list pages up to 2,000 rows (comment at line 56). `items`, derived from the same inputs, is already memoized.
findings.fix: `const coverage = useMemo(() => agreements ? agendaCoverage(agreements, events) : 'full', [agreements, events])`, and the same for `withoutTerm`.

findings.rule: Performance: no inline style objects re-created in long lists
findings.problem: `const Separator = () => <View style={{ height: 12 }} />` allocates a new style object for every FlatList separator on every render. AgreementCollectionPresentation.tsx:48 is identical. MyApplications and the candidate list already use a StyleSheet entry.
findings.fix: Add `separator: { height: 12 }` to each file's StyleSheet and render `<View style={s.separator} />`.

findings.rule: List rows need stable keys; motion only on the thing that changed
findings.problem: The removable term chips are keyed by index. A tap removes the chip while its Press is still springing back from the 0.97 press-in scale. With index keys, that same Press instance now draws the next chip, so the neighbour appears shrunk and springs, while the removed chip's element survives under another value.
findings.fix: Key each chip by its value plus its occurrence among equal values (capabilityTerms keeps duplicates), e.g. key={`${value}\u0000${values.slice(0, index).filter(v => v === value).length}`}. Removing a chip then unmounts only that chip.
